judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Loose, chatty, slightly sloppy ('as token of my gratitude', 'ya'), a smuggler's aside about responsibilities; uneven lengths between the two asks read like real map text.

items.label: B
items.critique: Two neatly parallel asks, the second the stock 'Psst! Hey, you!' rogue with a 'Never been used! Well... hardly.' gag and 'Heh, heh, heh!' payoff; too tidy and symmetrical.

items.label: C
items.critique: Same template as B: solemn elder plus 'Psst' smuggler, 'quiet-like', 'Heh, heh, heh...'; the '--' scene description and polished setting exposition feel composed rather than Nox.

items.label: D
items.critique: The stocks and the pig line are charming, but again the 'Psst' prisoner, 'A deal's a deal', 'Heh, heh, heh... Now you never saw me!' formula repeated across the packet.

items.label: E
items.critique: Breathless, run-on, comma-missing ('[Place], the village north of here and kidnapped'), generic thanks lines; exactly Westwood's Ogre-raid register.

items.label: F
items.critique: Wordy-yet-plain innkeeper voice, 'I surmise', exact gold sums (250, 100), 'savage scum'; the uneven structure and genial digressions are Westwood's.

items.label: G
items.critique: Tithe-chest ask is neat, but the 'Psst! Goin' up the hill, are ye?' informant with a cheese joke and 'Heh, heh...' is the repeated rogue template; the outcome cites a cellar door never set up.

items.label: H
items.critique: Escort quest with accept/refuse branches, the hungry-Ogre stomach joke and 'the menfolk cannot live without us': classic Nox broad humour and plain mechanics talk.

items.label: I
items.critique: Parallel garrison ask and 'Psst! Over here by the bars!' prisoner, pie gag, 'a deal's a deal', 'Heh, heh, heh'; 'Soldiers without pay are surly soldiers' is a writerly aphorism.

items.label: J
items.critique: Terse functional opener, sponsorship/petition mechanics, a ruby key handed over in-line, a 'foul little urchin' aggravating bats: the odd specific quest logic of Westwood's campaign.

tells: The new texts reuse one template: a solemn civic ask plus a 'Psst! Hey, you!' rogue offering a sword or shield, ending 'Heh, heh, heh' and 'a deal's a deal'. Westwood's pairs are not built in parallel.
New texts are symmetrical and tidy: matched lengths, a gag in every second ask, clean punctuation. Westwood's are uneven, sometimes very short, with small grammar slips and run-ons.

Westwood's quests carry game mechanics plainly (accept/refuse branches, keys, petitions, exact gold sums like 250 or 100), while the new ones lean on atmosphere ('our boats come home blind in the fog') and aphorisms.
Westwood's thanks lines are often generic ('Please accept this as a token of my appreciation!'); the new outcomes always pay off the setup's joke.
